rv.q: And yet, the sneaky truth is that this wild, thrilling, go-for-broke, genuinely hilarious musical comedy remains one of the funniest shows in the West End.
Directed with terrific zap and zestful precision.
This is a tremendous show, as accomplished as it is funny.
Their satirical musical The Book of Mormon, written in league with Avenue Q's Robert Lopez, wowed Broadway in 2011.
At its best, The Book of Mormon is indecently funny.
This show is the real deal, but as such it does it a disservice to make too many ridiculous claims for it.
While this one, beneath its jollity, is morally null and — without seeming to notice it — pretty racist.

The Book of Mormon is far, far cleverer, far kinder, far more nuanced than that, and one of its many surprises is that it sent an enraptured, ecstatic audience home with an odd sense of having come, somehow, to really like Mormons.
If you are not too easily offended and are willing to leave your sense of morality at the theatre door, you will be entertained.

All in all, I can see why the house was full on a Wednesday evening a year after the show opened - a small theatre, exclusive tickets and an incredible cast make this witty, tongue in cheek triumphant musical still one of the hottest spots in town.
Heaven in the West End does exist and it can be found at the Prince of Wales Theatre.
Slick, funny and full of barnstorming numbers this satirical assault is also a buddy movie at heart

cn.t: South Park creators deliver an irreverent yet surprisingly sweet musical that's indecently funny and expertly crafted, though a few critics find it overhyped or less shocking than advertised. A feel-good Broadway sensation with jaunty songs.
